title: The ? Shortcut
goal: Parse a number and double it. Invalid input must return an error, not a panic or a fake value.
hints: The function's return type already says Result - someone upstream wants to KNOW about failures.
unwrap panics on garbage; unwrap_or(0) hides it inside a plausible number. Only one choice tells the caller the truth.
explanation: All three compile. unwrap() turns bad input into a panic - the garbage test dies instead of failing gracefully. unwrap_or(0) is subtler poison: "x" quietly becomes Ok(0) and the error test fails because no error exists anymore - the caller can't tell garbage from zero. The ? operator forwards the ParseIntError to the caller, matching the signature's promise exactly: one character, honest function.
